newsitem.title: USA: Ford '96 minority purchases top $1.96 billion.
newsitem.headline: Ford '96 minority purchases top $1.96 billion.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Monday it purchased $1.96 billion worth of automotive components and services from U.S. minority suppliers in 1996 -- the highest amount in its history and $162 million more than in 1995.
Ford also said it has established a target to source at least five percent of its annual U.S. purchases by the year 2000 from minority suppliers or approximately $2.5 billion.
Last year's $1.96 billion represented about four percent of Ford's 1996 U.S. purchases.

Ford said four areas, in particular, helped the company increase its U.S. minority purchases in 1996: powertrain and chassis components; electrical and electronic components; industrial materials; and construction, utility and building services purchases.

"Ford Motor Company has made a strong commitment to the minority community and is backing that commitment with real dollar purchases from outstanding minority suppliers," said Carlos Mazzorin, Ford's top purchasing executive.
In addition to the five percent sourcing target, Ford has launched a number of initiatives to assist minority suppliers attain long-term success.

Among those initiatives is a financial and technical assistance program designed to assist Ford's preferred minority suppliers during periods of robust growth, which provides suppliers with funding to help pay the interest on new loans that support growth as a result of Ford business.
